review.plain: Gives anyone injured or whose property is damaged by violations of section 127A or section 39 of chapter 265 a civil action for injunctive relief, damages and attorney fees, and makes parents liable for judgments against their minor children.
Defacing a milk dealer's name or mark on a milk can without the owner's consent, or using such a can in business with intent to defraud, is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: effaces, alters or covers over, or procures to be effaced, altered or covered over, the name, initial or device of any dealer in milk, marked or stamped upon a milk can
detains or uses in his business any such can having the name, initial or device of any dealer in milk so marked or stamped thereon

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $10

crimes.act: Effaces, alters or covers over, or procures to be effaced, altered or covered over, the name, initial or device of any dealer in milk, marked or stamped upon a milk can
ways: procures to be effaced, altered or covered over
conditions: Without the consent of the owner

crimes.act: Detains or uses in his business any such can having the name, initial or device of any dealer in milk so marked or stamped thereon
conditions: Without the consent of the owner

review.plain: An inmate of a state correctional institution who wilfully and maliciously destroys or injures property of the commonwealth there, or of anyone furnishing materials for prisoners' work, may get up to 3 years in state prison.
acts: destroys or injures the property of the commonwealth at such correctional institution, or the property of any person who furnishes materials for the employment of the prisoners

shared.who: An inmate of a correctional institution of the commonwealth

penalties.penalty: Up to 3 years in state prison

crimes.act: Destroys or injures the property of the commonwealth at such correctional institution, or the property of any person who furnishes materials for the employment of the prisoners

review.plain: A prisoner at a jail or house of correction who wilfully and maliciously injures or destroys public property or materials furnished for prisoners' work may be imprisoned for 6 months to 2½ years.
acts: injures or destroys any public property or any materials furnished for the employment of prisoners in such jail or house of correction

shared.who: A prisoner at a jail or house of correction

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment for not less than 6 months nor more than 2½ years

crimes.act: Injures or destroys any public property or any materials furnished for the employment of prisoners in such jail or house of correction

review.plain: Allows a person caught wilfully injuring a fruit or forest tree or committing malicious mischief on Sunday to be arrested without a warrant and held until a complaint is made, but not beyond the following day.
Wilfully killing pigeons on, or frightening them from, beds made for netting them, within 100 rods, except on one's own land, is punishable by up to 1 month in prison or a $20 fine, plus damages.
acts: kills pigeons upon, or frightens them from, beds which have been made for the purpose of taking them in nets, by any method, within one hundred rods of the same

penalties.penalty: Up to 1 month imprisonment or a fine of up to $20

consequences: Liable for the actual damages to the owner or occupant of such beds

crimes.act: Kills pigeons upon, or frightens them from, beds which have been made for the purpose of taking them in nets, by any method, within one hundred rods of the same
exceptions: On land lawfully occupied by himself

review.plain: Unlawfully entering a Humane Society house, boat house or hut and damaging or taking property, or damaging or trespassing on its life-saving property, is punishable by up to 6 months in prison or a $200 fine.
acts: unlawfully enters a house, boat house or hut which is the property of the Humane Society of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and wilfully injures, removes or carries away any property belonging to said society
injures or unlawfully uses or commits any trespass upon the property of said society which is intended or kept for the purpose of saving or preserving human life
commits any trespass upon such house, hut or boat house

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $200 or up to 6 months imprisonment

consequences: One half of any fine paid goes to the person who gives information upon which a conviction is obtained

crimes.act: Unlawfully enters a house, boat house or hut which is the property of the Humane Society of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and injures, removes or carries away any property belonging to said society
exceptions: The penalties do not apply to persons for whose use said boats, houses and other property are intended and kept

crimes.act: Injures or unlawfully uses or commits any trespass upon the property of said society which is intended or kept for the purpose of saving or preserving human life
exceptions: The penalties do not apply to persons for whose use said boats, houses and other property are intended and kept

crimes.act: Commits any trespass upon such house, hut or boat house
exceptions: The penalties do not apply to persons for whose use said boats, houses and other property are intended and kept

review.plain: Mooring a vessel to a U.S. government buoy, beacon or floating guide in state waters is punishable by a fine of up to $50; wilfully destroying, injuring or removing one, by up to 3 months or a $100 fine.
acts: moors or in any manner makes fast a vessel, scow, boat or raft to a buoy, beacon or floating guide placed by the government of the United States in the navigable waters of the commonwealth
destroys, injures or removes any such beacon or guide

consequences: One third of all fines goes to the complainant and two-thirds to the commonwealth

crimes.act: Moors or in any manner makes fast a vessel, scow, boat or raft to a buoy, beacon or floating guide placed by the government of the United States in the navigable waters of the commonwealth

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $50

crimes.act: Destroys, injures or removes any such beacon or guide

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $100 or up to 3 months imprisonment

review.plain: Knowingly raising a river or stream by a dam so that it floods or injures a lawfully existing mill in the commonwealth, without right, is punishable by up to 6 months in prison or a $1,000 fine.
acts: causes the water of a river or stream so to be raised as to flow upon or injure a mill lawfully existing in the commonwealth and belonging to a citizen thereof

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,000 or up to 6 months imprisonment

crimes.act: By erecting or maintaining a dam, either within or without the commonwealth, causes the water of a river or stream so to be raised as to flow upon or injure a mill lawfully existing in the commonwealth and belonging to a citizen thereof
conditions: Without right as against the owner of such mill
exceptions: Cases in which the courts of the commonwealth have jurisdiction to abate a dam so raised or maintained

review.plain: Wilfully damaging a dam, reservoir, canal, mill gear or mill machinery, or wilfully or wantonly draining or blocking water in a mill pond or reservoir, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: breaks down, injures, removes or destroys a dam, reservoir, canal or trench, or a gate, flume, flashboards or other appurtenances thereof, or a wheel, or mill gear, or machinery of a water mill or steam mill
draws off the water contained in a mill pond, reservoir, canal or trench, or obstructs such water from flowing out of the same

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $500 and up to 2 years in jail

crimes.act: Breaks down, injures, removes or destroys a dam, reservoir, canal or trench, or a gate, flume, flashboards or other appurtenances thereof, or a wheel, or mill gear, or machinery of a water mill or steam mill
Draws off the water contained in a mill pond, reservoir, canal or trench, or obstructs such water from flowing out of the same
ways: obstructs such water from flowing out

review.plain: Wilfully and without right damaging or disabling machinery or equipment used to carry water for agricultural purposes is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: damages or renders unusable machinery or equipment used in the transmission of water for agricultural purposes

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $500 and up to 2 years in jail

crimes.act: Damages or renders unusable machinery or equipment used in the transmission of water for agricultural purposes

review.plain: Removing or altering a motor vehicle or trailer's identifying numbers, or selling vehicles or parts knowing the numbers were altered, is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison; stealing another's registration plate, up to 2½ years.
acts: removes, defaces, alters, changes, destroys, obliterates or mutilates or causes to be removed or destroyed or in any way defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated, the identifying number or numbers of a motor vehicle or trailer
sells, transfers, distributes, dispenses or otherwise disposes of or attempts to sell, transfer, distribute, dispense or otherwise dispose of any motor vehicle or trailer or motor vehicle part
buys, receives, possesses, or obtains control of a motor vehicle, trailer, or motor vehicle part
takes and carries away the registration plate that is attached to the vehicle of another or is assigned by the registry of motor vehicles to another

terms: "Identifying number or numbers": the manufacturer's number or numbers identifying the motor vehicle, trailer or motor vehicle part as required to be contained in an application for registration by section two of chapter ninety, including the identifying number or numbers as restored or substituted under authority of section thirty-two A of said chapter ninety or similar law of another state
consequences: The court reports a conviction or delinquency adjudication to the registrar of motor vehicles, who shall revoke immediately the license or right to operate motor vehicles; an appeal does not stay the revocation

No new license or reinstatement until 60 days after revocation for a first offense, or 1 year after revocation for any subsequent conviction or adjudication, unless the prosecution is finally terminated in the person's favor

crimes.act: Removes, defaces, alters, changes, destroys, obliterates or mutilates or causes to be removed or destroyed or in any way defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated, the identifying number or numbers of a motor vehicle or trailer
ways: causes to be removed, destroyed, defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,000 or up to 3 years in state prison, or both

crimes.act: Sells, transfers, distributes, dispenses or otherwise disposes of any motor vehicle or trailer or motor vehicle part
exceptions: Unless authorized by law to do so
knowledge: Knowing or having reason to believe that the identifying number or numbers to said motor vehicle, trailer, or vehicle part have been so removed, defaced, altered, changed, destroyed, obliterated, or mutilated

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,000 or up to 3 years in state prison, or both

crimes.act: Buys, receives, possesses, or obtains control of a motor vehicle, trailer, or motor vehicle part
exceptions: Unless authorized by law to do so
knowledge: Knowing or having reason to believe that an identifying number to said vehicle, trailer, or vehicle part has been removed, obliterated, tampered with, or altered

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500 or up to 2 years in a house of correction, or both

crimes.act: Takes and carries away the registration plate that is attached to the vehicle of another or is assigned by the registry of motor vehicles to another

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $500 nor more than $1,000 or up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or both

review.plain: Removing or altering the identifying numbers of any machine or electrical or mechanical device to conceal it, defraud, hinder competition or hide a crime, or selling such a device knowingly, is punishable by up to 1 year in jail.
acts: removes, defaces, alters, changes, destroys, obliterates or mutilates or causes to be removed or destroyed or in any way defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated, the identifying number or numbers of any machine or any electrical or mechanical device
sells or otherwise disposes of or attempts to sell or otherwise dispose of a machine or an electrical or a mechanical device

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500 or up to 1 year in a jail or house of correction, or both

crimes.act: Removes, defaces, alters, changes, destroys, obliterates or mutilates or causes to be removed or destroyed or in any way defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated, the identifying number or numbers of any machine or any electrical or mechanical device
ways: causes to be removed, destroyed, defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated
intent: With intent thereby to conceal its identity, to defraud the manufacturer, seller, or purchaser, to hinder competition in the areas of sales and servicing, or to prevent the detection of a crime

crimes.act: Sells or otherwise disposes of a machine or an electrical or a mechanical device
knowledge: Knowing or having reason to believe that the identifying number or numbers of the same have been so removed, defaced, altered, changed, destroyed, obliterated or mutilated

review.plain: Selling, offering to sell, or soliciting offers to buy a master key for more than one motor vehicle, knowing it will be used illegally, is punishable by up to 1 year in prison, a $500 fine, or both.
acts: sells or offers to sell or solicits offers to purchase a master key designed to fit more than one motor vehicle

knowledge: Knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that said key will be used for an illegal purpose

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500 or up to 1 year imprisonment, or both

crimes.act: Sells or offers to sell or solicits offers to purchase a master key designed to fit more than one motor vehicle

review.plain: Makes anyone who uses odometer-altering devices, resets odometers, or knowingly drives with a disconnected odometer to defraud liable in a civil action for triple damages or $1,500, and treats it as unfair competition.
Turning back or readjusting a motor vehicle's speedometer or odometer to misrepresent its mileage to a buyer is punishable by a $500 to $1,000 fine, 30 days to 2 years in jail, or both.
acts: turns back or readjusts the speedometer or odometer thereof

intent: With the intent to misrepresent to a prospective or eventual purchaser the number of miles traveled by a motor vehicle

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $500 nor more than $1,000, or not less than 30 days nor more than 2 years in a jail or house of correction, or both

crimes.act: Turns back or readjusts the speedometer or odometer of a motor vehicle

review.plain: A business buying copper line wire or scrap copper wire that fails to record each purchase and seller in a book open to police inspection faces a fine of up to $50.
acts: violates any provision of this section

shared.who: A person in the business of purchasing copper line wire or scrap copper wire

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $50

crimes.act: Fails to enter in a book kept for that purpose a description of the same, the quantity purchased, the purchase price and a name and address of the seller

Fails to keep said book at all times open to the inspection of the chief of police of a city or town or any other officer having similar duties or any officer authorized by either of them, or a state police officer

review.plain: Gold, silver and platinum buyers must record purchases of $50 or more in a book open to police, and sellers must show photo ID; violations bring up to 1 year in prison, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: violates any provision of this section

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,000 or up to 1 year imprisonment, or both

crimes.act: Fails to enter in a book kept for that purpose a description of the item, quantity purchased, the purchase price and the name and address of the seller
conditions: The purchase price of such item is at least $50
crimes.who: A person in the business of purchasing gold, silver or platinum

crimes.act: Fails to keep said book at all times open to the inspection of the chief of police of a city or town or of any other officer having similar duties or any officer authorized by either of them, or a state police officer
crimes.who: A person in the business of purchasing gold, silver or platinum

crimes.act: Fails to show to the buyer prior to said sale identification which includes a photograph of said seller
crimes.who: A person who sells gold, silver or platinum

review.plain: Defines "article" or "recorded device," "audiovisual recording function," "motion picture theater" and "owner" for sections 143A to 143H on unauthorized recordings.
Knowingly copying sound recordings without the owner's consent to sell, rent or use them for profit, or knowingly selling such copies, is a crime punished as provided in section 143E.
acts: transfers or causes to be transferred any sound recorded on a phonograph record, disc, wire, tape, film, videocassette or other article on which such sound is recorded
sells any such article

penalties.penalty: Set in section 143E of chapter 266

crimes.act: Directly or indirectly by any means, transfers or causes to be transferred any sound recorded on a phonograph record, disc, wire, tape, film, videocassette or other article on which such sound is recorded
conditions: Without the consent of the owner
intent: With intent to sell, rent or transport, or cause to be sold, rented or transported, or to use or cause to be used for profit through public performance such article on which such sound is so transferred

crimes.act: Sells any such article
knowledge: With the knowledge that the sound thereon has been so transferred without the consent of the owner

review.plain: Recording a live performance without the owner's consent for commercial gain, or selling, renting or possessing such recordings knowing they were unauthorized, is a crime punished as provided in section 143E.
acts: records or causes to be recorded a live performance
advertises, sells, rents, transports or causes to be advertised, sold, rented or transported, or possesses for any of such purposes, a recording of a live performance

intent: For commercial advantage or private financial gain

penalties.penalty: Set in section 143E of chapter 266

crimes.act: Records or causes to be recorded a live performance
knowledge: With knowledge that such recording is without the consent of the owner

crimes.act: Advertises, sells, rents, transports or causes to be advertised, sold, rented or transported, or possesses for any of such purposes, a recording of a live performance
ways: causes to be advertised, sold, rented or transported
possesses for any of such purposes
knowledge: With the knowledge that the live performance was recorded without the consent of the owner

review.plain: Knowingly making, renting, selling, transporting or possessing for sale recorded devices whose packaging lacks the true name and address of the transferor, for commercial gain, is punished as provided in section 143E.
acts: manufactures, rents, sells, transports, or causes to be manufactured, rented, sold or transported, or possesses for purposes of sale, rental or transport, any recorded device the outside packaging of which does not clearly and conspicuously bear the true name and address of the transferor of the sounds or images contained thereon

intent: For commercial advantage or private financial gain

penalties.penalty: Set in section 143E of chapter 266

crimes.act: Manufactures, rents, sells, transports, or causes to be manufactured, rented, sold or transported, or possesses for purposes of sale, rental or transport, any recorded device the outside packaging of which does not clearly and conspicuously bear the true name and address of the transferor of the sounds or images contained thereon
ways: causes to be manufactured, rented, sold or transported
possesses for purposes of sale, rental or transport

review.plain: States that sections 143A to 143C do not apply to persons lawfully entitled to use the sounds or images, to radio or television broadcasts or archival preservation, or to law enforcement officers acting lawfully.

Sets penalties for violating sections 143A to 143C on unauthorized recordings: up to 1 year in a house of correction, rising to up to 5 years in state prison for 1,000 or more sound or 65 or more audiovisual recordings.
acts: violates any provision of section 143A to section 143C, inclusive

penalties.penalty: Up to 1 year in the house of correction or a fine of up to $25,000, or both

penalties.if: the offense involves less than 1,000 but not less than 100 unlawful sound recordings or less than 65 but not less than 7 unlawful audio visual recordings
penalties.penalty: Up to 2 years in the house of correction or a fine of up to $100,000, or both

penalties.if: the offense involves not less than 1,000 unlawful sound recordings or not less than 65 unlawful audio visual recordings
penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison or a fine of up to $250,000, or both

crimes.act: Violates any provision of section 143A to section 143C, inclusive

review.plain: Knowingly operating a recording device in a movie theater during a showing to unlawfully record the film without consent is punishable by up to 2 years in a house of correction, or 5 years in state prison for repeat offenses.
acts: operates an audiovisual recording function

intent: With the intent to unlawfully record the motion picture

penalties.penalty: Up to 2 years in the house of correction or a fine of up to $100,000, or both
Up to 5 years in state prison or a fine of up to $250,000, or both

crimes.act: Operates an audiovisual recording function
conditions: In a motion picture theater while a motion picture is being exhibited
Without the consent of the owner or lessee of the motion picture theater
exceptions: Local, state or federal law enforcement officers employing an audiovisual recording function during the lawful exercise of law enforcement duties

review.plain: Gives a defense to false arrest or false imprisonment claims for reasonably detaining a person at a movie theater on reasonable grounds of a section 143F recording violation.
Allows the court, upon a conviction under sections 143A to 143C or 143F, to order forfeiture or destruction of the recordings and equipment used, stayed pending appeal.
Carrying away or converting a stamped plastic or wire milk case or milk-products container without the owner's permission is punishable by a fine of $10 to $100.
acts: carries away or converts to his own use a plastic or wire milk case or a plastic or wire container for milk products which has been indelibly stamped with the name of a milk dealer or association of milk dealers

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $10 and not more than $100

crimes.act: Carries away or converts to his own use a plastic or wire milk case or a plastic or wire container for milk products which has been indelibly stamped with the name of a milk dealer or association of milk dealers

review.plain: Intentionally concealing a public record of the commonwealth or a local government, intending to permanently deprive it of the record, is punishable by a fine of up to $500.
acts: conceals upon his person or otherwise any record of the commonwealth or a political subdivision thereof

intent: With the intention of permanently depriving said commonwealth or said political subdivision of its use

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500

crimes.act: Conceals upon his person or otherwise any record of the commonwealth or a political subdivision thereof
conditions: The record is a record of the commonwealth or a political subdivision thereof, as defined in section three of chapter sixty-six

review.plain: Wilfully dumping solid waste in another's commercial disposal container without the owner's or custodian's consent is punishable by a fine of $100 to $1,000.
acts: deposits solid waste in a commercial disposal container of another

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $100 nor more than $1,000

terms: "Solid waste": garbage, refuse, trash, rubbish, sludge, residue or by-products of processing or treatment of discarded material, and any other solid, semi-solid or liquid discarded material resulting from domestic, commercial, mining, industrial, agricultural, municipal, or other sources or activities, but not solid or dissolved material in domestic sewage

crimes.act: Deposits solid waste in a commercial disposal container of another
conditions: Without the consent of the owner or other person who has legal custody, care or control thereof
